{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned phenotyping strings (e.g., Angina; ICD10 I20; PheCode 411.3; and one time-to-event variant). Within that family, PGS001262 has the strongest incremental signal (incremental AUROC 0.0098; PGS R2 0.01304) and uses only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), with a reasonably large validation sample (n=49,472), so it is the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. Limitation: these snpnet scores come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (\"across 813 traits\"), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; meanwhile several newer ICD10/PheCode-based models (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527 and PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057) lack clearly PRS-only metrics (mostly full-model C-index or OR only, with covariates sometimes unknown), making them hard to compare directly and preventing a high-confidence, clearly dominant selection."}
